explanation: When the model looked at the abstract, it saw the words "massive ascites" and "abnormal peritoneal tissue" — these are big, fluid-filled pockets in the belly (ascites) and the lining of the belly and pelvis. The model thought, "Oh, that's not good! " It's like when you have too much water in your bathtub — it's not healthy. Then, it noticed that the patient's belly lining (peritoneal) didn't look normal. It's as if there's a hole in the bottom of your bathtub, and it's leaking. This leaking, or "peritonitis," is not good either. So, the model thinks, "Uh-oh, this could be a problem. " That's why it classified this as a "digestive system disease. "
